issues.description: Method Course.addRating(stars:) has inconsistent return type across artifacts: the problem statement (problem_statement.md line 15) describes implementing an instance method addRating(stars:) but does not specify a return value; the template implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift line 24) declares the method as `func addRating(stars: Int)` (Void); the solution implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift line 25) defines `func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool` returning a Bool success flag. This inconsistency leaves students uncertain whether they should return a Bool or not, and may cause mismatches with tests or expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred if you want to signal success/failure): update the problem statement to state that addRating(stars:) returns Bool indicating whether the rating was accepted, change the template signature to `func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool { ... }`, and keep the solution as-is. Option B (if you prefer a void API): update the solution to implement a Void method `func addRating(stars: Int)` and adjust any tests or documentation that rely on a Bool return. Ensure Client examples and tests are updated to match the chosen signature.
